Microchip Technology updates its networking and storage products to better support AI and HPC workloads
Expanded data center portfolio will help customers address multiple infrastructure challenges, the company said
Microchip Technology has expanded its data center solutions portfolio by enhancing its networking and storage offerings to support artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications.
The additions include the Switchtec PCIe 6.0 Low-Lane-Count (LLC) switch, an updated Flashtec PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 SSD controller, and an enhanced Adaptec SmartRAID 4300 family of NVMe RAID storage accelerators.
Microchip said the LLC switch has been designed for space- and power-constrained systems, providing up to 64 PCIe Gen 6 lanes and 32 ports, with flexible two-, four-, eight-, and 16-bifurcation options. The switch also incorporates direct memory access technology to support peer-to-peer data transfers between connected devices while reducing host CPU involvement, the company said, adding that it has also extended the same PCIe multicast and partitioning functions to the switch as can already be found in Microchip’s larger PCIe Gen 6 switch product portfolio.
Meanwhile, the updates to Microchip’s storage products will see its Flashtec PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 SSD controller offer advanced virtualization, quality of service management, and programmability, to help optimize performance across enterprise, hyperscale, and AI deployments.
The company’s family of Adaptec SmartRAID 4300 NVMe RAID storage accelerators has also been upgraded, offering improved storage security and data protection, while minimizing downtime. Microchip has further added self-encrypting drives with both local and remote key management in RAID 6 and RAID 60 configurations for increased resiliency and security.
“Customers are looking for technology partners that can address multiple challenges across the infrastructure stack while helping simplify design and accelerate deployment,” said Brian McCarson, corporate VP and GM of Microchip’s data center solutions unit. “By continuing to expand our portfolio, we're providing the building blocks needed to create more efficient, secure, and adaptable platforms for today’s increasingly distributed and data-intensive computing environments.”

That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Quintauris and Microchip Technology join forces to grow RISC-V® adoption
Engagement also brings Quintauris benchmarking and software integration services to Microchip’s RISC-V development pipeline
Quintauris and Microchip Technology have entered into a partnership to support the advancement of RISC-V® by contributing to industry efforts that improve interoperability, software portability and consistency. Quintauris was founded to enable compatible RISC-V-based products, provide reference architectures, and help establish solutions to be widely used across various markets.
“Microchip embodies decades of trust and leadership in embedded computing,” said Pedro Lopez, CEO of Quintauris. “This collaboration marks another major step forward in the advancement of RISC-V, and we are honored to partner with Microchip on this journey.”
Quintauris supports semiconductor vendors by helping ensure their RISC-V-based designs meet expected use-case performance and compliance requirements before they reach production.
For Microchip, the collaboration is expected to help reduce manual validation efforts and shorten the path from design to silicon.
“Our customers are increasingly evaluating RISC-V for MCU applications and want confidence that the ecosystem will support their products for the long term,” said Greg Robinson, corporate vice president of Microchip’s MCU, wireless and development tools business units. “Through our collaboration with Quintauris, we are helping advance the standards, software foundations and validation practices that help reduce development risk and support greater compatibility across the RISC-V ecosystem.”
Quintauris continues to expand its ecosystem of industry leaders working together to accelerate the adoption of RISC-V and strengthen the path from development to production.
Quintauris is a global provider of RISC-V-based products. Founded in 2023, Quintauris develops profiles, reference architectures, and software components which enable compatibility and help establish RISC-V solutions to be widely used across various industries.
Founded by leading semiconductor players such as Bosch, Infineon, Nordic Semiconductor, NXP, Qualcomm, and STMicroelectronics, Quintauris’ mission is to accelerate the global adoption of RISC-V, the open standard Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), enabling the development of next-generation processors for automotive, industrial, and IoT applications.

While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Elektrobit and Microchip Collaborate on Pre-Integrated AUTOSAR Solutions for Next-Generation Automotive Platforms
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:30 AM CDT 3 min read
Collaboration combines Elektrobit's AUTOSAR software and tooling with Microchip's automotive microprocessor platforms to help automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers reduce integration effort, lower development risk and accelerate time to market
ERLANGEN, Germany and CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Elektrobit, a global expert in automotive software, and Microchip Technology Inc., a broadline supplier of semiconductors committed to making innovative design easier through total system solutions, today announced a collaboration to simplify and accelerate AUTOSAR-based software development for automotive manufacturers and suppliers using Microchip automotive platforms.
Elektrobit and Microchip Collaborate on Pre-Integrated AUTOSAR Solutions for Next-Generation Automotive Platforms
As the automotive industry moves toward software-defined vehicles (SDV), OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers are under increasing pressure to shorten development cycles while maintaining safety, quality and flexibility. By combining Microchip's automotive hardware platforms with Elektrobit's AUTOSAR software, tooling and automation capabilities, the two companies are enabling customers to establish a production-ready software foundation faster and more efficiently.
The collaboration provides customers with access to pre-integrated AUTOSAR Microcontroller Abstraction Layer (MCAL) software based on Elektrobit's market-proven EB tresos portfolio, helping development teams get started more quickly while reducing software integration complexity and project risk. The combined solution allows developers to focus more quickly on application development and vehicle differentiation rather than foundational software integration.
"By integrating Microchip automotive platforms with Elektrobit's AUTOSAR expertise and tooling, we are helping customers streamline development and accelerate adoption of next-generation automotive architectures," said Mark Reiten, senior corporate vice president, licensing, memory products and intelligent compute business units, Microchip. "Together, we are making it easier for developers to move from platform evaluation to production deployment."
As part of the unified automation-first approach, Elektrobit applies integration-as-code to turn repeatable Classic AUTOSAR integration work into reusable, executable logic so teams can deliver faster and scale capacity through automation. This supports advanced workflow automation and lays the groundwork for future AI-assisted software configuration and development processes.
"Automotive manufacturers are seeking ways to accelerate software innovation while reducing development costs and complexity," said Jaganathan Rajagopalan, vice president, head of strategy and portfolio, Elektrobit. "Our collaboration with Microchip combines proven automotive software foundations with ready-to-use hardware support, enabling customers to bring SDV innovations to market faster and with lower integration risk."
The collaboration also expands support across a growing range of Microchip automotive platforms. Elektrobit has successfully enabled EB tresos AutoCore OS and EB tresos AutoCore Generic modules on Microchip's SAMA5 series of microprocessors, making the solution available for immediate customer adoption, with support for additional platforms expected to follow as the collaboration evolves.
The companies plan to focus initial market activities on high-growth automotive segments in Asia, including the rapidly evolving two-wheeler market, while also supporting broader automotive opportunities across Asia and North America.
Elektrobit is the trusted partner in the transition to the software-defined vehicle (SDV). With over 35 years of award-winning automotive software expertise, Elektrobit's innovative portfolio and comprehensive SDV ecosystem empower OEMs, Tier 1s, along with ODMs and Big Tech to build future-ready solutions with speed and confidence. Its SDV building blocks include operating systems, middleware, embedded software, digital cockpit solutions, engineering services and development workflows – driving faster innovation and seamless integration across the vehicle lifecycle. Elektrobit software powers over five billion devices in more than 630 million vehicles worldwide. It is a wholly owned, independently operated subsidiary of AUMOVIO.
Microchip Technology Inc. is a broadline supplier of semiconductors committed to making innovative design easier through total system solutions that address critical challenges at the intersection of emerging technologies and durable end markets. Its easy-to-use development tools and comprehensive product portfolio support customers throughout the design process, from concept to completion. Headquartered in Chandler, Arizona, Microchip offers outstanding technical support and delivers solutions across the industrial, automotive, consumer, aerospace and defense, communications and computing markets. pages.text:

Microchip Expands Space Power Portfolio with New Radiation-Tolerant GaN Point-of-Load Converter
Microchip Technology Inc.
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 3 min read
Microchip Technology Inc.
Power device delivers 20A of continuous current in a compact form factor for new space and traditional space applications
CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the POL-05-20S-T, a radiation-tolerant, Point-of-Load (POL) converter, designed to address the demanding power requirements of space processing applications. The new device uses Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices to deliver up to 20A of output current with high efficiency and power density.
The converter is supplied in a compact, 25g surface-mount package measuring 1.51" x 1.51" x 0.45". By delivering 20A in this footprint, the device helps engineers manage the size, power and energy constraints that accompany increasingly capable onboard processing systems. The GaN-based design is intended to provide a combination of high efficiency, high power density and continuous current capability for challenging space power applications.
"Space designers are integrating increasingly powerful digital processing, creating demand for compact power solutions that can respond quickly, while operating reliably in harsh environments," said Ronan Dillon, senior director of Microchip's high-reliability and RF business unit. "The POL-05-20S-T extends our space power portfolio with a high-current GaN solution that helps customers achieve high power density, design flexibility and system-level reliability."
The POL-05-20S-T is designed for high-current, fast-transient applications such as for the core voltage rails of FPGAs, microcontrollers, ASICs and other processing-intensive digital loads. It combines a synchronous buck topology with current-mode control to support fast current transients and stable operation. With a wide input range of 4.75V to 13.2V and adjustable 0.7V to 5V output, the device offers flexibility to address multiple power rails and system architectures.
Designed for harsh radiation environments, the POL-05-20S-T has electrical parameters specified before and after irradiation up to a Total Ionizing Dose (TID) of 50 krad. The device is characterized for Single Event Effects (SEE) up to a Linear Energy Transfer (LET) of 43 MeV·cm²/mg. It operates from −55°C to +100°C at full load, supporting systems exposed to wide temperature variations over the course of a mission.
To support reliable power delivery, the POL-05-20S-T incorporates remote sensing, undervoltage and overvoltage protection, soft start, an enable pin and power-good indication pin. Adjustable output voltage, a wide input range and output droop regulation further help designers tailor the converter to high-current loads requiring tight voltage regulation and rapid transient response.
Microchip delivers a comprehensive space power suite that is part of an end-to-end solution for space system designers, including EMI filters, DC-DC converters, point-of-load regulators, Hi-Rel discrete components, FPGAs and the PIC64-HPSC High-Performance Spaceflight Computing devices. Built on decades of space heritage, the portfolio helps customers simplify development, reduce design risk and accelerate deployment of mission-critical space systems. For more information about Microchip's space solutions, visit the website.
The POL-05-20S-T is now available in production quantities. You can purchase directly from Microchip or contact a Microchip sales representative or authorized worldwide distributor.

Can NVTS' Alliance With Microchip Accelerate Its AI Power Growth?
Navitas Semiconductor NVTS is expanding its AI data center opportunity through its collaboration with Microchip Technology. The companies have developed an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for next-generation AI data center racks. The solution combines Microchip's digital power control and security technologies with NVTS' GaN power devices and is aligned with the Open Compute Project's 800V DC standard. The reference design includes hardware, software and design documentation to help data center developers reduce design time and bring new power systems to market faster.
The reference design uses NVTS' 650V GaNFast FETs and Microchip's dsPIC33AK digital signal controllers and TA100 CryptoAuthentication device. The system is designed to deliver up to 96% peak efficiency at full load, with a power density of 2,100 watts per cubic inch. It directly converts 800V DC to 6V DC by combining the 800V-to-50V and 50V-to-6V stages into a single converter. This approach is aimed at improving power conversion efficiency while supporting compact rack power systems.
The collaboration comes as AI data centers require higher power density and more efficient power delivery. Navitas has been focusing on this market as part of its broader shift toward high-power applications. In the second quarter of 2026, NVTS' high-power markets grew more than 50% year over year, while AI infrastructure is expected to account for more than one-third of total sales by the end of 2026. The company is also working on multiple AI data center programs tied to the transition toward 800V architectures.
The Microchip collaboration could help NVTS strengthen its position as more data center operators adopt 800V power systems. By combining NVTS' GaN technology with Microchip's digital control and security capabilities, the companies are offering customers a more complete solution for AI rack power. As 800V adoption expands, the new reference design could help NVTS gain additional design opportunities in the growing AI data center market.
The company faces strong competition from ON Semiconductor ON and STMicroelectronics STM in the race to supply high-voltage solutions for AI data centers.
ON is expanding its presence in AI data center power as the industry moves toward 800V DC architectures. The company expects AI data center revenues to more than double in 2026, while silicon carbide revenues from AI data center applications are expected to grow nearly 60% year over year. The company expects its high-voltage revenues to accelerate as data centers adopt 800V DC distribution, increasing demand for its power solutions across the AI power tree.
STMicroelectronics is another semiconductor company gaining from rising AI data center power demand. The company reported 50% year-over-year growth in communication equipment and computer peripherals in the second quarter, supported by its AI-related customer programs. STM is already supplying microcontrollers, high-voltage power and analog products for the power stage of cloud AI systems and is building a pipeline for low-voltage power solutions. The company expects data center revenues to exceed $1 billion in 2026 and $2 billion in 2027 if current trends continue.

Microchip Expands Data Center Portfolio to Meet Evolving AI Infrastructure Demands
Microchip Technology Inc.
Microchip Technology Inc.
New connectivity, storage and acceleration solutions help address performance, security and scalability challenges across modern computing architectures
CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As AI workloads drive demand for more scalable and flexible data center architectures, organizations are looking for faster, more efficient ways to move, store and protect data. Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) is helping to address these needs by expanding its portfolio of data center solutions with new innovations in PCIe® connectivity, NVMe® storage and acceleration that support high-performance computing infrastructure.
"Customers are looking for technology partners that can address multiple challenges across the infrastructure stack while helping simplify design and accelerate deployment," said Brian McCarson, corporate vice president and GM of Microchip's data center solutions business unit. "By continuing to expand our portfolio, we're providing the building blocks needed to create more efficient, secure and adaptable platforms for today's increasingly distributed and data-intensive computing environments."
Designed to bring PCIe Gen 6 connectivity to space- and power-constrained platforms, the Switchtec™ PCIe 6.0 Low-Lane-Count (LLC) switch provides up to 64 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, 32 ports and flexible x2, x4, x8 and x16 bifurcation options. Integrated Direct Memory Access (DMA) supports efficient peer-to-peer data movement between connected devices while reducing host CPU involvement. Like Microchip's larger Switchtec Gen 6 devices, the LLC switch features PCIe Multicast and partitioning capabilities along with robust security through hardware root of trust and secure boot technologies. The new device delivers PCIe Gen 6 capabilities with a smaller, lower power footprint to extend support to a broader range of data center and intelligent edge applications.
To address the industry's requirements for secure, scalable and AI-optimized storage infrastructure, Microchip is updating its Flashtec® SSD controller portfolio with an enhanced version of the PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 controller. Building on the controller's high-performance, power-optimized architecture, the updated device adds support for Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite (CNSA) 2.0 to help customers prepare for emerging post-quantum security requirements. Dual-port capability enables highly available storage architectures through redundant data paths and load balancing, while advanced virtualization, Quality of Service (QoS) management and flexible programmability help optimize performance. Together, these enhancements extend the Flashtec platform's ability to address evolving NAND technologies, high-capacity SSD designs and next-generation enterprise, hyperscale and AI deployments.
Microchip is also expanding the capabilities of its Adaptec® SmartRAID 4300 family of NVMe RAID storage accelerators with a series of enhancements designed to address practical operational needs. The updates are focused on strengthening storage security, minimizing downtime, expanding data protection and simplifying deployment across a wider range of environments. Self-encrypting drives (SEDs) with both local and remote key management, and RAID 6 and RAID 60 options have been added for increased resiliency and security. Broader platform compatibility is enabled through support for Linux®, Debian, Ubuntu® and Microsoft® Windows® 11 environments. Additional updates such as dynamic NVMe configuration for in-service management, persistent event logging and peer-to-peer rebuild support for greater CPU offload help reduce management overhead while minimizing service disruption. StorageCore API support further expands integration flexibility, enabling customers to incorporate SmartRAID management into third-party tools through in-band host applications as well as customized out-of-band BMC management frameworks.
The latest additions reflect the company's ongoing commitment to advancing the performance, availability and security of next-generation computing platforms. Visit the website to learn more about Microchip's full portfolio of data center solutions.
Microchip's data center portfolio is supported by a suite of development and management tools, including ChipLink software for configuration, diagnostics, telemetry and debug of PCIe switches. Additional support includes software for device monitoring, configuration and firmware management, Flashtec NVMe controller development resources and Adaptec storage management software.

Microchip Technology (MCHP) Stock Is Up, What You Need To Know
What Happened?
Shares of analog chipmaker Microchip Technology (NASDAQ:MCHP) jumped 4.3% in the afternoon session after the stock continued to rally as the company introduced a new line of advanced digital power monitors the previous day.
As detailed in a company press release, Microchip launched the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V digital power monitors, which are specifically designed for 48V power applications to measure accumulated energy use and provide transient headroom to withstand sudden voltage spikes.
These new chips are designed to help engineers build smarter and more resilient high-voltage electronic systems, allowing commercial customers to better manage energy draw and protect sensitive equipment. By expanding its lineup of power-management products, Microchip is directly targeting the growing industrial demand for robust 48V architectures, prompting investors to continue bidding up the stock as they digest the expanded total addressable market.
Moving forward, the market is treating this product launch as a steady step in capturing higher-margin power management market share, though sustaining this momentum will depend on how quickly customers actually integrate the new chips into their upcoming hardware designs.
The shares were trading at $77.97, up 4.4% from the previous close.

Microchip Technology's shares are very volatile and have had 23 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock dropped 3% on the news that the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.14% following strong September business activity data that raised expectations for tighter Federal Reserve interest rate policy. Technology and semiconductor shares came under selling pressure in premarket trading on September 24, according to TipRanks. The 10-year Treasury yield is the return investors earn for lending money to the U.S. government for a decade. When it rises, safer bonds become more attractive compared with stocks.
That shift matters most for technology companies. Their valuations often rest on profits expected years in the future. Higher yields reduce what those future earnings are worth in today's dollars. The jump in yields followed strong September business activity data. Solid economic readings can lead investors to expect the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates higher, or raise them further, to prevent the economy from overheating. Tighter policy increases borrowing costs and can weigh on growth-focused sectors.
Other pressures added to the selling. Elevated crude oil prices raised concerns about inflation. There is also uncertainty over trade and tariffs on advanced semiconductors ahead of the summit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Tariffs are taxes on imported goods, and any new restrictions could affect chipmakers that depend on global supply chains and sales to China. Together, rising rates, energy costs, and trade uncertainty created a difficult setting for the sector.
Microchip Technology is up 19.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $77.97 per share, it is still trading 24.2% below its 52-week high of $102.92 from May 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Microchip Technology's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $938.95.

Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

ERLANGEN, Germany and CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Elektrobit, a global expert in automotive software, and Microchip Technology Inc., a broadline supplier of semiconductors committed to making innovative design easier through total system solutions, today announced a collaboration to simplify and accelerate AUTOSAR-based software development for automotive manufacturers and suppliers using Microchip automotive platforms.
Elektrobit and Microchip Collaborate on Pre-Integrated AUTOSAR Solutions for Next-Generation Automotive Platforms
As the automotive industry moves toward software-defined vehicles (SDV), OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers are under increasing pressure to shorten development cycles while maintaining safety, quality and flexibility. By combining Microchip's automotive hardware platforms with Elektrobit's AUTOSAR software, tooling and automation capabilities, the two companies are enabling customers to establish a production-ready software foundation faster and more efficiently.
The collaboration provides customers with access to pre-integrated AUTOSAR Microcontroller Abstraction Layer (MCAL) software based on Elektrobit's market-proven EB tresos portfolio, helping development teams get started more quickly while reducing software integration complexity and project risk. The combined solution allows developers to focus more quickly on application development and vehicle differentiation rather than foundational software integration.
"By integrating Microchip automotive platforms with Elektrobit's AUTOSAR expertise and tooling, we are helping customers streamline development and accelerate adoption of next-generation automotive architectures," said Mark Reiten, senior corporate vice president, licensing, memory products and intelligent compute business units, Microchip. "Together, we are making it easier for developers to move from platform evaluation to production deployment."
As part of the unified automation-first approach, Elektrobit applies integration-as-code to turn repeatable Classic AUTOSAR integration work into reusable, executable logic so teams can deliver faster and scale capacity through automation. This supports advanced workflow automation and lays the groundwork for future AI-assisted software configuration and development processes.
"Automotive manufacturers are seeking ways to accelerate software innovation while reducing development costs and complexity," said Jaganathan Rajagopalan, vice president, head of strategy and portfolio, Elektrobit. "Our collaboration with Microchip combines proven automotive software foundations with ready-to-use hardware support, enabling customers to bring SDV innovations to market faster and with lower integration risk."
The collaboration also expands support across a growing range of Microchip automotive platforms. Elektrobit has successfully enabled EB tresos AutoCore OS and EB tresos AutoCore Generic modules on Microchip's SAMA5 series of microprocessors, making the solution available for immediate customer adoption, with support for additional platforms expected to follow as the collaboration evolves.

CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the POL-05-20S-T, a radiation-tolerant, Point-of-Load (POL) converter, designed to address the demanding power requirements of space processing applications. The new device uses Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices to deliver up to 20A of output current with high efficiency and power density.
The converter is supplied in a compact, 25g surface-mount package measuring 1.51" x 1.51" x 0.45". By delivering 20A in this footprint, the device helps engineers manage the size, power and energy constraints that accompany increasingly capable onboard processing systems. The GaN-based design is intended to provide a combination of high efficiency, high power density and continuous current capability for challenging space power applications.
"Space designers are integrating increasingly powerful digital processing, creating demand for compact power solutions that can respond quickly, while operating reliably in harsh environments," said Ronan Dillon, senior director of Microchip's high-reliability and RF business unit. "The POL-05-20S-T extends our space power portfolio with a high-current GaN solution that helps customers achieve high power density, design flexibility and system-level reliability."
The POL-05-20S-T is designed for high-current, fast-transient applications such as for the core voltage rails of FPGAs, microcontrollers, ASICs and other processing-intensive digital loads. It combines a synchronous buck topology with current-mode control to support fast current transients and stable operation. With a wide input range of 4.75V to 13.2V and adjustable 0.7V to 5V output, the device offers flexibility to address multiple power rails and system architectures.
Designed for harsh radiation environments, the POL-05-20S-T has electrical parameters specified before and after irradiation up to a Total Ionizing Dose (TID) of 50 krad. The device is characterized for Single Event Effects (SEE) up to a Linear Energy Transfer (LET) of 43 MeV·cm²/mg. It operates from −55°C to +100°C at full load, supporting systems exposed to wide temperature variations over the course of a mission.
To support reliable power delivery, the POL-05-20S-T incorporates remote sensing, undervoltage and overvoltage protection, soft start, an enable pin and power-good indication pin. Adjustable output voltage, a wide input range and output droop regulation further help designers tailor the converter to high-current loads requiring tight voltage regulation and rapid transient response.
Microchip delivers a comprehensive space power suite that is part of an end-to-end solution for space system designers, including EMI filters, DC-DC converters, point-of-load regulators, Hi-Rel discrete components, FPGAs and the PIC64-HPSC High-Performance Spaceflight Computing devices. Built on decades of space heritage, the portfolio helps customers simplify development, reduce design risk and accelerate deployment of mission-critical space systems.
